_doc.word_in_agent_messages_all_runs: Every run in the default config, not only the study sets (word_scan.py): for the word in each prompted label's own name, runs whose agent messages (assistant-role reasoning and completions) match it, by label, by label for prompted runs, and by model for runs labeled exactly normal. System and user messages are not searched.
_doc.label_word_check: For each prompted label checked, its runs and the normal runs whose agent messages contain the label's word, and the AUROC of that yes/no check against all normal runs, (1 + TPR - FPR) / 2.
_doc.dataset: Counts over public MALT's default config, from index.parquet.
_doc.spine_signals: Organic sample, from signal_scan.py. signals: the five regexes and their union, positives = 62 organic reward-hacking runs, controls = 52 same-task normal runs. recall_k/recall_n = positives flagged, fpr_k/fpr_n = controls flagged, *_ci = Wilson 95% intervals, fisher_p_two_sided = Fisher exact test on the 2x2 table, fisher_p_task_stratified = exact conditional test stratified by task, pos_hits_expected_within_tasks = positive hits expected if hits were spread within each task in proportion to run counts (below recall_k means the signal leans to controls), hits_by_task = per-task counts. matches says what the regex matched. read_write_split: the two file-call signals split into runs with at least one read-mode match (_read) and runs whose matches are all writes (_write_only). raw_args_all_roles: the same regexes on raw JSON-encoded tool arguments of every role, the scope of an earlier draft. organic_pos, organic_pos_cot, organic_pos_nocot, prompted_pos, organic_by_task and label_totals describe all of public MALT, not the sample: organic_pos counts all 87 unprompted runs with any behavior label, so its no-chain-of-thought count differs from the sample's 27.
_doc.monitor_settings: Model and request settings behind every monitor score.
_doc.summary blocks: n_pos/n_neg = runs scored; auroc = Mann-Whitney AUROC, ties counted half; auroc_ci95 = stratified bootstrap percentile interval (positives and controls resampled separately, B=4000, seed 20261113); mean_pos/mean_neg = mean suspicion (0-100); at_fpr_5pct/at_fpr_10pct = operating point that flags runs scoring above flag_if_above, chosen as the lowest threshold with fp <= max_fp = floor(5% or 10% of controls); tp/recall = positives flagged, recall_ci95 = Wilson interval, fp/fpr = controls flagged (the realized false-positive rate).
_doc.channel_ablation: Sabotage sample. Prompted sabotage study, 60 sabotage + 60 normal runs, sabotage prompt, three input channels. *_paired_differences: AUROC difference on the same runs with a paired stratified bootstrap.
_doc.cot_obfuscation: Sabotage sample. Chain-of-thought-only channel on the 80-run subset under the clean config and MALT's four obfuscations; the default rows reuse the channel-ablation scores. *_paired_vs_default: AUROC of the config minus AUROC of default on the same runs.
_doc.subset_vs_held_out: Channel-ablation AUROC on the 80-run obfuscation subset and on the 20 sabotage + 20 normal runs left out of it.
_doc.organic_monitor: Organic sample. Reward-hacking prompt, full channel, 62 positives vs 52 controls. at_union_fp_count: operating point with no more flagged controls than the deterministic union (decoded scan); at_raw_args_union_fp_count: the same at the raw-argument scan's union count.
_doc.organic_monitor_restricted: models_with_controls: positives from models that also have controls, vs all controls. metr_reward_hacking_labels_only: positives carrying bypass_constraints or ignores_task_instructions, vs all controls. hacks_without_chain_of_thought, hacks_from_models_without_controls, those_are_the_same_runs and controls_without_chain_of_thought: the two confounds and whether they coincide.
_doc.organic_per_label_flagged: For each label, n = positives carrying it (multi-label runs count under every label), and tp/recall with a Wilson interval at the 5%, 10% and union-count operating points of organic_monitor.
_doc.keyword_baseline: Score 1 if the monitor's input matches \bsabotag\w* (case-insensitive), else 0, on the same runs the monitor scored. pos_with_word/neg_with_word = runs that keep the word; substring_without_word_boundary = runs containing 'sabotag' only inside a longer word.
_doc.masked_ablation: Every match of \bsabotag\w* replaced by '[word removed]' and the rep re-scored. Reps without a match are identical to the unmasked input and keep their unmasked score. pos_masked/neg_masked = reps that changed and were re-scored; reason_mentions_removal = masked reps whose one-line monitor reason mentions the removal (the marker appears only in positives, so it is a cue of its own); masked_minus_unmasked = paired AUROC difference.
_doc.masked_ablation_neutral: As masked_ablation, but each match is replaced by a plain verb of the same form ('sabotaging' -> 'changing'; mask_reps.py --neutral), so the masked input carries no marker that the normal runs lack. The two full 120-run sets only.
_doc.other_intent_words_after_neutral_mask: Runs per class whose neutral-masked input still matches each term (case-insensitive). Descriptive only: it shows how often the reasoning still states the plan in other words once the masked word is gone.
_doc.task_overlap: Distinct tasks among positives and controls, tasks shared by both classes, runs on shared tasks, and AUROC restricted to runs on shared tasks.
_doc.system_preamble_after_cut: The system-message text the monitor still sees in the sabotage study after the cut at 'Instructions:'. Counts of distinct texts per class, texts shared by both classes, word counts, word-level similarity of the two most common texts and the sizes of the spans where they differ. No text is stored.
_doc.transcript_share_seen: seen_chars / total_chars per rep: characters of message text and tool-call arguments that reached the monitor, over the same count for the whole transcript. Median and minimum per class, median transcript size, and how many reps were cut to head + tail.
_doc.dropped_calls_in_final_scores: Monitor calls without a score in the score files used above.
_doc.api_usage: Every real API call of the study, per call log and in total: in_tok/out_tok from the API's usage field, no_score = calls that returned no score, hit_max_tokens = calls stopped by max_tokens, cost at the listed prices.
